title: Derived triangle and orthogonality of an exact localization kernel
statement: Let \(\mathcal C\) be an abelian category with its derived category, and let \(F,H:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C\) be additive functors preserving finite limits and finite colimits. Suppose \(\epsilon:F\to\mathrm{id}\) and \(\eta:\mathrm{id}\to H\) form a short exact sequence at every object. The derived presentation [def-sf-recollement-presentation-data] has functors \(D(F),D(H)\), with maps obtained by localizing the given degreewise maps and their canonical factorization isomorphisms. For every \(K\in D(\mathcal C)\), these two maps extend to a distinguished triangle. Separately, let \(L:\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D:R\) be an adjunction between abelian categories with derived categories. Assume \(L,R\) are additive and preserve finite limits and colimits, the counit is invertible, and the kernel of the unit is exact and additive. For all \(K,M\in D(\mathcal C)\) and \(n\in\mathbf Z\), the group \(\operatorname{Hom}(D(\ker\eta)(K)[n],D(LR)(M))\) is zero.

source.place: Integral sheaf localization and coefficient passage, steps 3–10

proof.text: Apply the standard derived triangle to the degreewise short exact sequence. Conjugate by the exact-functor factorization isomorphisms and transport along a representative complex. For orthogonality L kills the unit kernel by preservation of kernels and the triangle identity. Homology shows its exact derived image is zero; shifts remain zero. The localized adjunction gives the Hom vanishing.
